role: adversarial tester: vault-side receipt edge cases (duplicate ledger rows / unreadable vault file / FIFO)
invocation: timeout 10 env SHOKUNIN_ROOT=<empty-fleet> SOUJI_LEDGER=<case ledger under tests/vault/vadv-51/> tools/souji-verify.sh --stale-days 1 <target>

controls.conclusion: mode-000 file is genuinely unreadable by its owner (EACCES), so H1 exercises a real unreadable vault copy
raw sha256sum on a writer-less FIFO blocks (timeout rc 124); the tool must not hash non-regular files, and this harness timeout guard is load-bearing

cases.constructed: row1 full match (source sha + vault file + vault sha); row2 same source path, wrong vault_sha256
cases.oracle: SAFE(moved-to-obsidian): any row matching all four fields is a receipt per spec; winning row's vault copy verified live
cases.notes: first fully-matching row supplies the receipt; the mismatching duplicate is skipped with a note; 5 identical runs

cases.constructed: same two rows as G1, order reversed: mismatching row first, matching row second
cases.oracle: SAFE(moved-to-obsidian): a match anywhere wins; spec silent on duplicate precedence
cases.notes: scan continues past the mismatching row; outcome identical to G1 => order-independent, not first-row-only

cases.constructed: row1 same source path but stale source_sha256; row2 full match
cases.notes: stale first row does not block the later valid row

cases.constructed: two rows, SAME vault path, contradictory vault_sha256: wrong first, correct second
cases.oracle: SAFE(moved-to-obsidian): row agreeing with live vault hash wins; advisory
cases.notes: ground-truth-consistent row wins regardless of order

cases.constructed: control: both duplicate rows mismatch (wrong vault sha + missing vault path)
cases.notes: no matching row anywhere => NOT-SAFE, no false-SAFE

cases.constructed: two rows, both full matches, but each names a DIFFERENT vault copy (both byte-identical to source)
cases.oracle: SAFE(moved-to-obsidian): spec-conformant either way; observed first-row-wins
cases.notes: first fully-matching row wins; evidence names the winning vault; deterministic across 3 runs

cases.constructed: same two full-match rows as G6, order reversed: winner evidence should follow row order, not sort order
cases.notes: proves first-row-wins is positional (the alternate vault named by row1 supplies the evidence)

cases.constructed: row1 same source path, vault_path missing on disk; row2 full match
cases.notes: a dead first row does not block a valid second row

cases.constructed: ledger row fully matching a vault file whose mode is 000 (sha256sum EACCES)
cases.oracle: NOT-SAFE: vault hash cannot be verified, receipt fails
cases.notes: unreadable vault copy => sha unverifiable => NOT-SAFE; no crash, rc 0, deterministic

cases.constructed: ledger row fully matching but the SOURCE file itself is mode 000
cases.oracle: NOT-SAFE: source hash cannot be verified, receipt fails
cases.notes: unreadable source => source hash unverifiable => NOT-SAFE; advisory mirror of H1

cases.constructed: ledger row fully matching, vault_path is a FIFO (no writer); raw sha256sum on it blocks forever
cases.oracle: NOT-SAFE: FIFO is not a regular file; vault copy unverifiable
cases.notes: tool's -f guard skips the FIFO before hashing => no hang (rc 0, fast)

cases.constructed: FIFO passed as the CLI target itself, fresh mtime, ledger row present for it
cases.oracle: NOT-SAFE: FIFO target has no receipt; advisory
cases.notes: no hang on FIFO target either; -f guard skips it in the ledger branch; fresh mtime blocks stale

cases.constructed: row whose vault_path is a byte-identical copy sitting NEXT TO the source, not under any vault root
cases.oracle: conservative oracle NOT-SAFE (receipt claims moved-to-obsidian but copy is not in the vault); spec-silent
cases.notes: spec is silent on vault-root containment; tool trusts vault_path as given => SAFE observed (finding, not harness failure)

cases.constructed: row whose vault_path is a symlink resolving back to the source file itself
cases.oracle: conservative oracle NOT-SAFE: symlinked vault copy is not an independent preserved copy
cases.notes: sha256sum follows the symlink => hashes equal => SAFE observed; deleting the source would dangle the vault copy (false-SAFE candidate)

conclusions.g: Duplicate rows for one source path: the first FULLY-MATCHING row supplies the receipt (G6/G6R: both rows match but name different vault copies; reversing row order reverses the named winner, so precedence is positional = row order, not sort order); rows that mismatch source sha, vault sha or vault reachability are skipped with notes and never win (G1/G2/G3/G4/G7: a mismatching, stale, contradictory or dead row never blocks a later valid row). The outcome is order-independent (G1 match-first == G2 mismatch-first, byte-identical) and deterministic across repeated runs. SAFE is spec-conformant (a row matching all four fields is a receipt and its vault copy is verified live at run time); duplicate-row precedence itself is spec-silent, so conflict-safety is recorded as NOT-VERIFIED-by-spec rather than as a defect.
conclusions.h: chmod-000 vault file: file_sha fails (EACCES) => vault-sha-mismatch => NOT-SAFE(none), rc 0, no crash, deterministic across 3 runs. Unreadable source (H2) mirrors it: NOT-SAFE(source-sha-mismatch).
conclusions.i: FIFO as vault file: the tool's -f guard skips it before any hashing => vault-unreachable => NOT-SAFE(none), rc 0, no hang (raw sha256sum on the same FIFO hangs: control I0 rc 124). FIFO as CLI target (I2) also completes without hanging.
conclusions.advisory: X2 symlinked vault copy resolving to the source yields SAFE (false-SAFE candidate: removing the source dangles the vault copy). X1 vault_path outside any vault root also yields SAFE (spec-silent). Both are spec gaps, not harness failures.

notes: Binding cases: G1, G2, G6 (duplicate rows), H1 (unreadable vault file), I1 (FIFO vault file). Advisory: G3, G4, G5, G6R, G7, H2, I2, X1, X2.
Every tool invocation is wrapped in timeout 10; a timeout is counted as a hang (rc 124).
All fixtures and ledgers live under tests/vault/vadv-51/; the live ledger was header-only before and after (1 line(s)), tool sha unchanged, and the fixture manifest hash is unchanged across the run.
G1/G2/G3/G4/G5/X1/X2 targets are untracked fixture files inside this repo, so the pushed receipt is cleanly inapplicable and only the ledger/stale branches can yield SAFE.

Recommendation: add an explicit spec sentence for duplicate rows (first full match wins) and consider refusing vault copies that are symlinks resolving to the source, plus a vault-root containment note.
